name: Lever shear
description: A cast-iron bench shear with a long lever. Cuts sheet steel in straight lines or curves.
notes: A bench-mounted machine rather than a carried item; the size is only a placeholder. Modelled with the lever raised: a 300 by 240 mm foot plate, a 200 mm blade pair and a 0.9 m lever, 0.97 m tall. metal_shearing is a new quality name; no existing one covers cutting sheet metal. CHECK VOLUME: the box is mostly air round the raised lever; the reference's 18 L fits the frame and lever folded down.

name: Brazier
description: A steel fire bowl on three legs. Keeps a fire off the ground and away from anything that would catch.
notes: 550 mm across the bowl, 440 mm to the rim, with a bar grate and a loop handle each side. cooking carries the reference's cooking and boiling qualities. CHECK VOLUME: the box counts the open bowl and the space between the legs; the steel itself is a fraction of the reference's 30 L. Longest side x1.2 is the handles outside the 550 mm bowl.

name: Folding chair
description: A grey plastic seat and back on a steel tube frame. Folds flat to carry.
notes: Folded and standing: 420 mm wide, 890 mm tall and 80 mm deep, the seat folded up against the front legs. CHECK VOLUME: the box counts the gaps in the open frame; the folded panels alone match the reference's 5 L. Deploying it into a seat needs a placed-furniture state the drafts leave to the integration.

name: Butter churn
description: An oak barrel churn in a wooden stand, turned by a treadle and crank. Holds about ten litres of cream.
notes: A 340 mm barrel 240 mm across in a stand 460 mm tall and 610 mm long with the crank. The reference shows it as a keg; it has no longest side. churning is a new quality name. A machine that stands where it is used, so the size is only a placeholder. CHECK VOLUME: the box counts the open stand; the barrel itself holds about 13 L against the reference's 11.4 L.

name: Folding cot
description: An army camp bed folded for carrying: olive canvas between aluminium rails, legs folded under and strapped.
notes: Folded: 1 m long, 240 mm wide and 140 mm tall, with two webbing straps. Deploying it into a bed needs a placed-furniture state the drafts leave to the integration.

name: Deck chair
description: A wooden deck chair folded flat, with a blue and white striped canvas sling.
notes: Folded flat: three nested beech frames 1.2 m long and 600 mm wide, 90 mm thick. Deploying it into a seat needs a placed-furniture state the drafts leave to the integration.

name: Grass mat
description: A mat woven from dry grass and fibre, rolled up and tied. Spread out, it keeps meat off the dirt while butchering.
notes: Rolled: 900 mm long and 100 mm across, tied with two jute cords. work_surface is 1, as for every surface. CHECK VOLUME: the reference gives no longest side; a 100 mm roll is 7 L against its 2.5 L, kept so the roll reads at a glance.

name: Leather tarp
description: A large sheet of leather, rolled up and tied. Blood will not soak into it, which makes it a clean butchering surface.
notes: Rolled: 700 mm long and 100 mm across, with the loose edge showing and two rawhide ties. work_surface is 1, as for every surface. CHECK VOLUME: the reference gives no longest side; a 100 mm roll is 5.5 L against its 2.5 L, kept so the roll reads at a glance.

name: Manual tyre changer
description: A floor-bolted stand for taking tyres off rims and putting them back on, with a bead breaker lever and a foot pump.
notes: Three feet 1 m across, a wheel table 360 mm across on a 0.75 m post, a bead-breaker lever on a side post, a mounting bar and a foot pump. tire_changing is a new quality name. A machine that stays where it stands, so the size is only a placeholder. CHECK VOLUME: the box is mostly air round an open frame. Longest side x1.23 is the mounting bar swung out over the bead breaker.

name: Butchering rack
description: A folding steel frame for hanging a carcass off the ground, packed as three legs and a crossbar with hooks.
notes: Folded: three 600 mm galvanised legs and a crossbar strapped together, three S-hooks and a short chain. butchering follows earlier drafts. Deployed, it would become a placed rack; that state is left to the integration. Box/volume x0.45: the bundle is denser than the reference's 10 L, which counts the folded frame loosely.

name: Smoking rack
description: A folding steel rack of wire shelves for smoking meat and fish over a fire, packed flat with its legs on top.
notes: Folded: three wire shelves 900 by 400 mm stacked 70 mm deep, four legs and a hanger on top, two straps round it. smoking is a new quality name. Deployed, it would become a placed rack; that state is left to the integration.

name: Folding camp stove
description: A steel wood stove that folds into a flat case, with a carry handle and a short chimney clipped to its side.
notes: Folded: 320 by 210 mm and 45 mm thick, slotted grate panel on top, hinge knuckles at the front, chimney pipe clipped on. The reference lists no material; stainless steel is the usual build. cooking and boiling follow the brazier and the stock pot; it gives them once set up, which the drafts leave to the integration.

name: Screw press
description: A big oak frame press with a wooden screw and capstan bar. Squeezes oil from seed paste and juice from fruit.
notes: 1.2 m wide, 1.74 m tall, with a slatted basket in a drip tray and a 1.6 m capstan bar. pressing follows the hydraulic press. A machine that stays where it is built, so the size is only a placeholder. CHECK VOLUME and LENGTH: the box is mostly air inside an open frame; the reference's 2.5 m longest side would need a capstan bar longer than the press is wide, so the bar is kept at 1.6 m.

name: Folding camp table
description: A steel camp table folded into a flat slab, with a carry handle and two latches on the front edge.
notes: Folded: 900 by 540 mm and 40 mm thick, slatted top, folded legs underneath. Deploying it into a table needs a placed-furniture state the drafts leave to the integration.

name: Water mill
description: A paddle wheel on an oak axle turning a pair of millstones in a plank housing. Grinds grain into flour.
notes: A wheel 1.24 m across and 260 mm wide, millstones 500 mm across under a grain hopper, 1.3 m by 1.25 m by 1.05 m overall. milling is a new quality name. A structure built where it stands, so the size is only a placeholder. CHECK VOLUME: the box is mostly air round the open wheel; the reference's 22.5 L cannot hold a working wheel and stones, but its 120 kg and 1.5 m are kept close.
